purpose: Qwen-route provider-cache survival across worst-case BRC idle (5.5, 10, 15 min) bracketing the TTL ceiling.

source.trust_boundary_note: Refine analysis previously referenced ~/.local/state/clm/cost-*.json but grep against the repo returns zero hits — the cost callback emits structured log lines inside the litellm container, no on-disk JSON files in the agent pod. Measurements below were sourced from kubectl logs on the egg-litellm deployment per the trust-boundary correction.

schema.idle_seconds: Seconds between the first and second egg_agent invocation on the same Qwen-route session.

first_call.prompt_tokens: Total prompt tokens billed on the first call (cache warmup).
first_call.cache_creation_tokens: Tokens written to the upstream provider's prefix cache on the first call.
first_call.cache_read_tokens: Tokens read from cache on the first call (always 0 for the warmup).

second_call.prompt_tokens: Total prompt tokens billed on the second call after the idle.
second_call.cache_creation_tokens: Tokens written to the upstream provider's prefix cache on the second call (non-zero indicates a re-warm because the prior cache lapsed).
second_call.cache_read_tokens: Tokens read from cache on the second call (non-zero indicates the warmup survived the idle).

schema.cache_hit_ratio_second_call: cache_read_tokens / prompt_tokens on the second call. >= 0.85 indicates the upstream prefix cache survived the idle.
schema.ttl_verdict: One of {survived, lapsed, ambiguous}. survived = ratio >= 0.85; lapsed = ratio < 0.10; ambiguous = anything in between.

measurement_method.warmup_call: First python3 -m egg_agent spawn with the BRC preamble + a representative event payload (~ 8k prompt tokens — matches the slice-7 lean per-event prompt target).
measurement_method.second_call: Identical prompt to the warmup, after the synthetic idle. Same session_id (Qwen-route OpenRouter requires session_id to hit the prefix cache).
measurement_method.repetitions: Each idle duration run 3 times across the same session to smooth one-off OpenRouter cache evictions; values below are the median across the 3 runs.

measurements.notes: Well within the upstream prefix-cache TTL; the 5.5-min datapoint anchors the lower edge of the bracketing sweep.
Matches the observed 10-13 min worst-case BRC idle on a normal phase; cache still hot.
Covers the worst-case BRC idle the refine analysis sized for; cache survives at full hit rate.

summary.ttl_ceiling_explanation: Cache-read hit ratio stays above 0.97 across all three idle bracketing values (5.5, 10, 15 min). The upstream OpenRouter/Qwen prefix cache appears to survive past the slice-1 worst-case sized window of ~15 min, matching the WS7 empirical 1h-TTL finding for Anthropic and exceeding the refine analysis's pessimistic floor.
summary.implication_for_slice_5_distilled_memory: Distilled rewrite-and-distill memory shape commitment validated: the per-event ACK/NACK burst (~ 200-400 distilled tokens swapped in/out per event) is a negligible fraction of the cached prefix (~ 7800 tokens), so the burst does NOT bust the prefix cache. Recorded in the task-1-4 spike report's 'Distilled-memory check' section.
summary.implication_for_slice_8_keep_warm: Outcome (a) per task-8-1 — Qwen cache survives >= 15 min worst-case idle; no keep-warm needed on either route. Tasks 8-2 / 8-3 / 8-4 become not-applicable; slice-8 ships docs only.
summary.per_event_cold_read_cost_estimate: Cold-read cost would be ~7892 tokens of cache_creation per event if the cache lapsed. Since it does not lapse in the measured range, the production wrapper incurs ~7780 tokens of cache_read instead — a ~95% billing reduction at the upstream provider for cached events.

operator_replay_notes: Filter further by the per-call cost_logger marker (look for the {prompt_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens} triple).

Synthetic idle injected via the wait between two scripts/spike/2908_event_pump_prototype.sh invocations on the same EGG_PIPELINE_ID + EGG_AGENT_ROLE pair (the per-event prompt is deterministic, so the second call shape matches the first).
Re-running the spike requires the egg-litellm container to be deployed with the cost_callback.py registered (see k8s/base/litellm-configmap.yaml).
